Choose a hypothesis to test

Decision rule: shortlist a concept only after a local paid pilot supports repeat purchases and contribution margin. This site does not label any category a proven market gap.

Can the proposed sales cover costs?

Illustrative assumptions, not observed prices or a forecast. Edit every input for your concept. Values are not saved or sent to a server.

Formula: daily break-even sales = ceiling[monthly fixed costs ÷ (sale price − variable cost) ÷ trading days]. Include rent, wages, utilities and other overhead in fixed costs, and ingredients/materials, payment fees and other per-sale costs in variable cost. This simplified model excludes taxes, financing, capacity constraints and upfront fit-out costs unless included in your inputs.

First candidate for validation: a small-format food-service pilot. The snapshot identifies 13 spaces below 1,500 sqft estimated vacant for over a year; the separate permit file contains 15 cottage-food permits. Together they justify investigating space availability and voluntary operator interest, not predicting customers or assuming these spaces are food-ready. Validate permitted use, kitchen requirements, rent, nearby competitors, actual menu prices and repeat purchasing before a lease or grant decision.

Next evidence: run a voluntary, anonymous concept survey covering preferred product, acceptable price band and purchase frequency; record no names, contact details, free-text identifiers or exact locations. Test willingness to pay with an aggregate paid-pilot tally. Download an unfilled validation template — it is a research plan, not collected survey data.
